stem: The chemical properties of an element are related to the electronic configuration of its atoms.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Give the full electronic configuration of a fluorine atom.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Deduce the number of pairs of electrons in the second energy shell, $n = 2$, of an oxygen atom.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Draw the shape of the highest energy orbital that contains electrons in an atom of calcium.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Write an equation to represent the first ionisation energy of sulfur.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why the first ionisation energy of sulfur is less than the first ionisation energy of phosphorus.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
Arrange the three species $\text{F}^-$, $\text{Ne}$ and $\text{Na}^+$ in order of increasing radius.

Explain your answer.
